subject: On-site cluster intake: tenant mapping, node classes, and path-to-archive
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@heliohealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@heliohealth.com
Date: 2028-12-07T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Initial intake: on-prem cluster for inference pods

Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. We want to start formalizing requirements for the pilot cluster at our Austin site (3 racks). Immediate asks:

- Tenant mapping: we will host 3 product tenants initially (search, chat, embeddings). We need guidance on isolation (namespaces vs node segregation) given compliance constraints.
- Node classes: recommended GPU/CPU mix for steady inference load of ~60 qps aggregate with occasional bursts to 240 qps (90th percentile).
- Storage: hot cache (NVMe) for KV cache, medium-tier blockstore for model artifacts, archive for logs. Questions on PV classes, backup cadence, and retention for compliance.

I've attached a quick site inventory and a partial network diagram. Also copying procurement to flag any lead times.

Next step — could we get a consolidated proposed layout + a one-pager callout of configuration choices we should commit to for the pilot?

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
HelioHealth

Attachments: helio-site-inventory.xlsx (xlsx), helio-network-sketch.png (image)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-07T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: on-prem cluster for inference pods

Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks and the inventory. High level responses below; I'll attach a short layout and a PV-class capture doc after internal alignment. TL;DR recommendations:

1) Tenancy/isolation
- For the pilot, use namespace-level isolation for dev/test workloads and dedicate node classes for production tenants that require strict isolation or encryption at rest separation. That gives fast rollout while preserving an easy path to stricter tenant separation later.
- Map tenants to node labels (tenant=search, tenant=chat, tenant=embeddings) and use nodeSelectors + PodTopologySpread to reduce noisy neighbor risk.

2) Node classes
- Base node class: c6g-like (8 vCPU, 64GB) for control-plane + lightweight services.
- Inference GPU class: 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs per node (or 4x T4 in smaller footprint) for steady 60 qps. For burst headroom to 240 qps, configure a small burst pool (ephemeral preemptible nodes) sized to handle 2x baseline.
- Autoscaler profile: conservative scale-up (1.5x routing cushion) and aggressive scale-down for cost.

3) Storage & PV classes
- KV cache: local NVMe ephemeral volumes with cross-node replication at app layer; use a cached local path and fall back to blockstore for cold misses.
- Model artifacts: encrypted blockstore class (ext4/xfs on LVM), snapshot policy daily, lifecycle to cheaper object store for models older than 90 days.
- Logs/metrics: writable to a separate PV class copied to archive (S3-compatible) for compliance. Retention policy: 1 year hot, 7 years cold (we'll scope exact retention with compliance).

I'll loop Neha for specific PV class recommendations and an attachment with the proposed PVC templates and StorageClass names.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments (will follow): redwood-network-diagram-v2.pdf, pv-class-profiles.md

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-07T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: on-prem cluster for inference pods

Samir — quick additions on the storage side based on the inventory you shared:

- PV class names (suggested):
  * sc-fast-nvme (local-provisioner, no-volume-snapshot, ephemeral by design)
  * sc-encrypted-block (RBD/LVM backed, snapshot-enabled)
  * sc-archive-s3 (Object gateway via minio or direct S3 for offsite retention)

- Backup/DR: take nightly model snapshots to sc-encrypted-block and replicate weekly to sc-archive-s3. For critical model artifacts, enable 4-hour incremental checkpoints.

- Eviction/QoS: mark inference pods Guaranteed with requests aligned to node GPU fractional allocation to ensure stable scheduling. Reserve system CPUs for kubelet/CRI and node-exporter by setting kube-reserved and system-reserved.

I'll attach pv-class-profiles.md and a short sample StorageClass YAML set we recommend for the pilot. Laura — can you confirm whether Helio's on-site storage vendor supports CSI snapshots? That will affect snapshot cadence.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: pv-class-profiles.md (md)

From: HelioHealth Ops <ops+infra@heliohealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@heliohealth.com>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: 2028-12-07T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: on-prem cluster for inference pods

Neha / Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side before we lock the pilot BOM:

- Our storage vendor (DataForge) supports RBD and CSI snapshots, but they recommend weekly full snapshots for large volumes due to IO constraints. Is that compatible with the 4-hour incremental suggestion?
- Procurement: lead time on the proposed GPUs may be 8–10 weeks; can you outline an interim configuration using smaller T4-equivalent cards that we can migrate from?

Also — can we have a single-page decision table that lists the choices (e.g., sc-fast-nvme: ephemeral, sc-encrypted-block: daily snapshot) so procurement and our CISO can sign off quickly?

We're generally good to proceed once we get the snapshot cadence options and the interim GPU plan.

— ops team

Attachments: none

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: HelioHealth Ops <ops+infra@heliohealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-07T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: on-prem cluster for inference pods

Ops team — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Snapshot cadence: compatible. Use weekly full snapshots at the storage layer (DataForge) and enable 4-hour incremental checkpoints at the application/model level. That minimizes IO pressure while providing fine-grained restore points for recent model pushes. We'll document the restore window and RTO estimates in the one-pager.

- Interim GPU plan: yes — start with 4x T4 nodes sized as the "burst" pool with strict taints (gpu=burst). We'll run capacity tests in week 2 of the engagement and migrate to A10G-equivalent nodes as they arrive; Redwood's deployment manifests include a node-affinity translation script to rebind workloads.

Action items (owners):
- Jonas: produce 1-page decision table + network diagram (attached) and sample StorageClass YAMLs by EOD tomorrow.
- Neha: finalize pv-class profiles and sample PVC templates by Thursday.
- Marissa: loop in Solutions Engineering for on-site kickoff and scheduling (Marissa to propose dates).
- Samir: confirm procurement window and whether DataForge can accelerate snapshot IO for the pilot.

I'll attach the redwood-network-diagram-v2.pdf and the decision table draft in the Drive link. If that looks good we'll schedule a 30-minute call with procurement and your CISO to sign off.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-v2.pdf (pdf); decision-table-onepager.pdf (draft)
